title: Managing Telemetry Definitions on the Fly
short_title: Managing TM Definitions on the Fly (CCS5 dynamic HK)
status_notes: Conference paper; no event name, date or status is printed. The text says the new PUS standard ECSS-E-ST-70-41C (2016) 'has been published last year' (PDF p. 6), so it was written in 2017; the PDF metadata creation date is 27 February 2017. It was posted on ESA Indico event 180, which also hosts pecchioli-egs-cc-esoc and 1400-trifin-paper.
summary:
A six-page conference paper by Petro Kazmirchuk of Terma B.V. describing DYNHK, the 'dynamic housekeeping' feature of Terma's CCS5 central checkout software. On-board software can define new housekeeping or diagnostic report packets at run time through PUS service 3 telecommands, but a checkout system only recognises packets already described in its spacecraft reference database, so AIT engineers have had to hand-craft static definitions. DYNHK instead watches the uplinked TC(3,1)/TC(3,2) definition requests and TC(3,3)/TC(3,4) clear requests and creates or disables the matching SCOS-2000 MIB entries in memory, without interrupting the running test session.

The paper summarises the PUS-A service 3 sub-services and the content of their application data (SID, collection interval, parameter identifiers, NFA and supercommutated groups), and explains the CCS5 architecture: server and client consoles, the interface manager IFMGR, Tcl-based TOPE scripts, and in-memory MIBs that can be merged from several suppliers with a 'Source' column. It walks through the packet identification chain shared with SCOS-2000 (APID, type and subtype, PIC, PID, then PLF/VPD) and lists exactly which PID and VPD columns are filled for a new definition: PID_TPSD equal to the allocated SPID, PID_INTER from the collection interval, VPD positions from the parameter list and a REPEATER row for supercommutated groups. It also names the configuration that generic PUS leaves open (a scheduling rate in milliseconds, a TC-to-TM APID mapping and predefined PIC rows). For an engineer it is a concise worked mapping of PUS service 3 onto MIB tables.

contents.title: Housekeeping and diagnostic data reporting service
Overview of the dynamic housekeeping implementation in CCS5

key_points.text: Sub-services used: TC(3,1) Define New Housekeeping Parameter Report, TC(3,2) Define New Diagnostic Parameter Report, TC(3,3)/TC(3,4) Clear HK/Diagnostic Parameter Report Definitions, and the reports TM(3,25) and TM(3,26).

TC(3,1)/(3,2) application data hold the SID, a collection interval in units of the default HK scheduling rate (DIAG_MIN_INTERV) and the list of on-board parameter IDs with counters; SID together with APID and sub-service uniquely identifies a TM packet definition.

CCS5 loads MIB tables into memory where TOPE can read all tables and write some; multiple MIBs (e.g. from different suppliers) can be merged, with a special field 'Source' recording each MIB's origin.

DYNHK runs as the TOPE script DynHkMonitor.tcl on the CCS Server Console; after a TC(3,1)/(3,2) is verified it derives a definition, assigns a unique SPID and publishes it atomically to the server, all client consoles and IFMGR with CCS5::remote.

Redefining an existing SID disables the old definition and adds a new one with a new SPID, so SPID and TPSD are never reused within a session; packets for a cleared definition are archived as unknown.

Dynamic entries are tagged Source = 'DYNHK' and can optionally be saved as separate MIB files and reloaded in a later session, depending on whether the on-board software keeps its definitions across reboots.
Identification follows SCOS2000: APID from the CCSDS header, service type/subtype from the data field header, PI1/PI2 locations from PIC, SPID from PID, then packet contents from PLF and/or VPD.

VPD rather than PLF is used because TC(3,x) lists parameter IDs without offsets; VPD also allows variable-length strings, and CCS5 archives all VPD samples so retrieval does not depend on when a packet was (re-)defined.

Users must configure a 'schedulingRate' (to convert the collection interval to milliseconds for parameter expiry) and a TC-APID-to-TM-APID mapping, and must predefine PIC records because the SID is not directly referenced in the MIB ICD.

PID rows created: PID_TYPE 3, PID_STYPE 25 or 26, PID_APID from settings, PID_PI1_VAL/PID_PI2_VAL from the SID, PID_SPID from a user-configurable offset, PID_TPSD = SPID, PID_TIME = Y, PID_INTER from the collection interval, PID_CHECK = 1; clearing sets PID_VALID to false.
VPD rows: VPD_TPSD = PID_TPSD, VPD_POS 1..NPAR, VPD_NAME = the PCF_NAME whose PCF_PID equals the parameter ID; if NFA = 1 a REPEATER row is added with VPD_GRPSIZE = NPAR2 and VPD_FIXREP = NREP.
Planned next steps: a dedicated MMI to pick parameters and send TC(3,1)/(3,2) and TC(3,5), and support for the new service 3 sub-services of ECSS-E-ST-70-41C.
